question: What is the main goal of workplace ergonomics for nurses?

options.A: Reducing the operational costs of purchasing medical equipment
options.B: Fitting the work environment to the physical needs of the nurse
options.C: Minimizing the total number of staff required per hospital shift
options.D: Increasing the speed of entering patient data into computer systems

explanation: Ergonomics is all about shaping your workspace, tools, and tasks to fit you nicely so you don't wear out your body. You matter! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is ignoring ergonomics risky for bedside nurses?

options.A: It causes immediate software failures on electronic health record systems
options.B: It forces patients to wait longer for their routine medication schedules
options.C: It immediately results in disciplinary action from hospital management
options.D: It leads to chronic physical discomfort and long-term occupational disability

explanation: Small strains add up over time! Ignoring how you lift and sit can lead to stubborn aches and lasting back or joint issues down the road. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: What happens to your spinal discs when you stay in an awkward posture, like bending forward for too long?

options.A: They receive increased blood flow and enhanced nutritional support
options.B: They experience uneven pressure that can compromise structural integrity
options.C: They completely regenerate to compensate for the additional workload
options.D: They lock into a rigid position to protect the spinal cord from injury

explanation: Bending forward squishes one side of your spinal discs more than the other. Over time, that uneven squeeze can weaken them and cause trouble. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: What happens to your muscles when you hold a poor posture without moving for a long time?

options.A: Rapid muscle strengthening and improved endurance over time
options.B: Increased oxygen delivery to the surrounding soft tissues
options.C: Immediate relaxation of the nervous system and reduced tension
options.D: Restricted local blood flow and accelerated physical fatigue

explanation: When a muscle stays clenched in one position, it squeezes its own blood supply. Without fresh blood bringing oxygen, it gets tired super fast! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which common nursing task often leads to Carpal Tunnel Syndrome today?

options.A: Repetitive wrist flexion and extension during computer data entry
options.B: Standing upright for extended periods during surgical procedures
options.C: Lifting heavy patients without the assistance of mechanical devices
options.D: Pushing medication carts across uneven hospital floor surfaces

explanation: All that heavy typing and mouse clicking puts constant pressure on the nerve inside your wrist. Remember to give your hands a break! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: A nurse who constantly tilts their neck forward to look at low computer screens is most at risk for what?
explanation: Peering downward at a screen strains your neck bones and muscles, which can speed up wear and tear in the cervical spine over time. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: Where should the top of your computer monitor be placed for comfortable viewing?

options.A: Resting directly on the desk surface
options.B: Significantly higher than the user's head
options.C: To the extreme left or right of the keyboard
options.D: At or slightly below eye level

explanation: Keeping the top of the screen right at or just below your eyes lets you look straight ahead with a nice, relaxed neck. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: When adjusting your chair at a nursing station, what is the best position for your legs?

options.A: The toes barely touch the ground while the heels remain elevated
options.B: The feet rest flat on the floor with knees bent at a right angle
options.C: The legs dangle freely to promote active core muscle engagement
options.D: The knees are positioned much higher than the hips for stability

explanation: Flat feet and a 90-degree knee bend take the pressure off your thighs and keep your lower back happy while you chart. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why should you keep a mobile computer cart close to your body when pushing it down the ward?

options.A: It prevents the internal computer battery from losing its charge quickly
options.B: It minimizes excessive forward leaning and reduces lower back strain
options.C: It allows the nurse to lock the wheels automatically with their feet
options.D: It ensures the screen is close enough to read without wearing glasses

explanation: Keeping heavy loads close to your center of gravity saves your lower back from doing all the heavy lifting and leaning! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: What movement must you avoid when turning a heavy mobile medical cart around a tight corner?

options.A: Twisting the torso while keeping the feet planted
options.B: Walking slowly to maintain control over the equipment
options.C: Pivoting the entire body in the direction of travel
options.D: Using both hands firmly on the cart steering handles

explanation: Never twist your back while your feet stay glued to the floor! Pivot your whole body with your feet instead to protect your spine. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main reason your eyes feel dry and gritty after staring at a computer screen for a long time?

options.A: Direct contact with harsh chemical cleaning agents
options.B: Excessive tearing triggered by high screen brightness
options.C: A significant decrease in the normal blinking rate
options.D: Inadequate humidity levels inside hospital clinical wards

explanation: When we focus hard on screens, we forget to blink! Blinking is what keeps our eyes naturally moist and comfortable. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: What does the 20-20-20 rule help protect you against during long documentation shifts?

options.A: Stiffness in the cervical neck vertebrae
options.B: Lower back pain from poor chair height
options.C: Digital eye strain and visual fatigue
options.D: Severe carpal tunnel syndrome in the wrists

explanation: Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. It gives your eye muscles a well-deserved breather! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the recommended way to take a quick workplace micro-break during a busy shift?

options.A: A fifteen-minute rest period taken every two hours of work
options.B: A five-minute stretch session performed strictly at the end of a shift
options.C: A ten-minute relaxation break taken immediately after lunch
options.D: A thirty to sixty-second pause taken approximately every hour

explanation: You don't need a long break to reset! A tiny 30 to 60-second pause every hour is enough to shake off tension and keep you going. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: How do quick stretches during a clinical shift help you feel better?

options.A: They permanently cure pre-existing degenerative spinal conditions
options.B: They eliminate the need to ever sit down during documentation
options.C: They restore local blood flow and reduce accumulated muscle stiffness
options.D: They replace the requirement for formal physical therapy exercises

explanation: Stretching wakes up your muscles, gets the blood flowing again, and melts away the stiffness from standing or sitting too long. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)
